Fixtures for the OPf_PARENS check (parens_test.go). perl keeps one boolean
bit, OPf_PARENS (P in Concise), on the op a source paren enclosed; psc keeps
Paren on the node. Each snippet is compiled as a file of its own by the
pinned perl (corpus.pin's interpreter, 5.44.0), and the check compares, per
statement line, the ops perl marks P with the ops psc's Paren nodes map to.

A line `=== NAME [CLASS ...]` opens a fixture; its source runs to `--- perl`.
`--- perl` lists the ops perl marks P, one `LINE OP [VAR]` per row, or
`none` when perl keeps no P for the snippet; VAR is the variable an op
like padsv or ex-rv2sv reads. `#` lines quote perl 5.44.0's
-MO=Concise. The structural ops every block and loop carries P on (leave,
leaveloop, lineseq, scope, and the null over an `if`) are not listed: the
check excludes them on perl's side.

=== a declared list [list-op]
my ($a, $b) = @_;
--- perl
1 ex-list
# -        <1> ex-list lKPRM* ->4

=== a declared list and a list assignment [list-op]
our ($p, $q);
($p, $q) = (1, 2);
--- perl
1 ex-list
2 ex-list
2 ex-list
# -     <1> ex-list vKP ->2
# -        <1> ex-list lKP ->6
# -        <1> ex-list lKPRM* ->9

=== a declared one-element list [one-element-list]
my ($x) = @_;
--- perl
1 padsv $x
# -           <0> padsv[$x:1,2] sPRM*/LVINTRO ->-
# the ex-list over it is lK, with no P

=== a localised one-element list [one-element-list]
our $x;
local ($x) = 1;
--- perl
2 ex-rv2sv $x
# -           <1> ex-rv2sv sKPRM*/LVINTRO,1 ->-

=== a lexical in parens [scalar-op]
my $x;
my $z = ($x);
--- perl
2 padsv $x
# 5        <0> padsv[$x:1,3] sP ->6

=== a package variable in parens [scalar-op]
our $x;
my $z = ($x);
--- perl
2 ex-rv2sv $x
# -        <1> ex-rv2sv sKP/1 ->4

=== a lexical in doubled parens [doubled scalar-op]
my $x;
my $z = (($x));
--- perl
2 padsv $x
# 5        <0> padsv[$x:1,3] sP ->6, as with one pair

=== a comparison in doubled parens as a call argument [doubled call-arg]
sub ok {}
our $y;
ok((($y eq "x")));
--- perl
3 seq
# 8           <2> seq sKPM/2 ->9, as with one pair

=== a comparison in parens as a call argument [call-arg]
sub ok {}
our $y;
ok(($y eq "x"));
--- perl
3 seq
# 8           <2> seq sKPM/2 ->9

=== a call's parens around a parenthesised constant [call-arg doubled]
print ((1))+2;
--- perl
1 const
# 4           <$> const[IV 1] sP ->5

=== a call's parens around a constant [call-arg single-form]
print (1)+2;
--- perl
none
# 4           <$> const[IV 1] s ->5: print's pair is its call parens

=== a parenthesised list as a call's argument [ex-list call-arg]
sub f {}
f((1,2));
--- perl
2 ex-list
# -           <1> ex-list lKPM ->8

=== a qw list [qw]
my @a = qw(a b);
--- perl
1 ex-list
# -        <1> ex-list lKP ->6

=== a one-word qw list [qw]
my @a = qw(a);
--- perl
1 const
# 4           <$> const[PV "a"] sP ->5

=== a qw list in parens [qw doubled]
my @a = (qw(a b));
--- perl
1 ex-list
# -        <1> ex-list lKP ->6, as without the parens

=== return of a parenthesised list [absorbed]
sub r {
  return (1, 2);
}
--- perl
2 return
# -        <@> return KP ->-: return absorbed the list, and no list op is left

=== return of a doubly parenthesised list [absorbed doubled]
sub s {
  return ((1, 2));
}
--- perl
2 return
# -        <@> return KP ->-

=== return of a parenthesised constant [scalar-op]
sub t {
  return (1);
}
--- perl
2 const
# 2           <$> const[IV 1] sP ->3

=== if, else and do blocks [block]
our $x;
if ($x) {
  my $y = 1;
  $y++;
}
else {
  my $y = 2;
  $y++;
}
my $r = do { my $z = 1; $z };
--- perl
none
# c           <@> leave vKP ->d, u           <@> leave vKP ->d,
# k           <@> leave sKP ->l and -     <1> null vKP/1 ->d over the if's
# `and`: structural, excluded. A one-statement block is `scope vK`, no P.

=== for and while loops [loop]
for my $i (1, 2) {
  my $y = ($i);
  $y++;
}
our $x;
while ($x) {
  $x--;
  1;
}
--- perl
2 padsv $i
# 8                    <0> padsv[$i:2,6] sP ->9
# g     <2> leaveloop vKP/2 ->h and -              <@> lineseq vKP ->-, on
# each loop: structural, excluded

=== an arrow call's argument [single-form]
my $f = sub {};
our $x;
$f->($x);
--- perl
none
# -           <1> ex-rv2sv sKM/1 ->8: the pair is the call's

=== an arrow call's argument in doubled parens [doubled]
my $f = sub {};
our $x;
$f->(($x));
--- perl
3 ex-rv2sv $x
# -           <1> ex-rv2sv sKPM/1 ->8

=== an arrow call's arguments [single-form]
my $f = sub {};
$f->(1, 2);
--- perl
none
# -        <1> ex-list K ->a: the pair is the call's

=== an arrow call's arguments in doubled parens [doubled ex-list]
my $f = sub {};
$f->((1, 2));
--- perl
2 ex-list
# -           <1> ex-list lKPM ->9

=== an arrow call with no arguments [single-form]
my $f = sub {};
$f->();
--- perl
none
# -        <1> ex-list K ->8

=== not's parenthesised operand [single-form]
our $a;
my $r = not ($a == 1);
--- perl
none
# 5           <2> eq sK/2 ->6: the pair is not's

=== not's operand in doubled parens [doubled]
our $a;
my $r = not (($a == 1));
--- perl
2 eq
# 5           <2> eq sKP/2 ->6

=== a parenthesised not [scalar-op]
our $x;
my $r = (not $x);
--- perl
2 not
# 4        <1> not sKP/1 ->5

=== a list slice of an array [single-form]
my @a;
my @x = (@a)[0];
--- perl
none
# 9                 <0> padav[@a:1,3] l ->a: the pair is the slice's

=== a list slice of an array in doubled parens [doubled]
my @a;
my @x = ((@a))[0];
--- perl
2 padav @a
# 9                 <0> padav[@a:1,3] lP ->a

=== a list slice of a list [single-form]
my $x = (1,2,3)[1];
--- perl
none
# -           <1> ex-list lK ->9

=== a list slice of a list in doubled parens [doubled]
my $x = ((1,2,3))[1];
--- perl
1 ex-list
# -           <1> ex-list lKP ->9

=== a list slice of stat in doubled parens [doubled]
my $x = ((stat "/"))[2];
--- perl
1 stat
# 7              <1> stat lKP/1 ->8; `(stat "/")[2]` is stat lK

=== a list slice of caller in doubled parens [doubled]
my $x = ((caller))[2];
--- perl
1 caller
# 6              <0> caller[t2] lP ->7

=== a list slice of a parenthesised element and a comma [doubled]
my $x = ((0),)[0];
--- perl
1 const
# 6              <$> const[IV 0] sP ->7; `(0,)[0]` is const[IV 0] s

=== an arrow call's parenthesised argument and a comma [doubled]
my $f = sub {};
$f->((0),);
--- perl
2 const
# 7           <$> const[IV 0] sPM ->8: the inner pair is the 0's

my $v = ($x && 1);
--- perl
2 null
# -        <1> null sKP/1 ->6

# -        <1> null sKP/1 ->6

=== a parenthesised and [logical]

=== a parenthesised ternary [logical]
our $x;

2 null
# -        <1> null sKP/1 ->6

=== a parenthesised do block [logical]
my $v = (do { 1 });
--- perl
1 null
# -        <1> null sKP*/1 ->4

=== a parenthesised && in void context [logical]
our $x;
($x && 1);
--- perl
2 null
# -     <1> null vKP/1 ->5

=== a parenthesised && beside a parenthesised variable [logical]
our $x;
my $v = ($x && 1) + ($x);
--- perl
2 null
2 ex-rv2sv $x
# -           <1> null sKP/1 ->6
# -           <1> ex-rv2sv sKP/1 ->7

=== two lexicals, one in parens [scalar-op]
my ($x, $y);
my $z = ($x) + $y;
--- perl
1 list
2 padsv $x
# -     <@> list vKP ->4
# 5           <0> padsv[$x:1,3] sP ->6

=== a declared list in void context [list-op]
my ($x, $y);
--- perl
1 list
# -     <@> list vKP ->4

=== a declared one-element our list [one-element-list]
our ($p);
--- perl
1 rv2sv $p
# -     <1> rv2sv vKP/OURINTR,1 ->3

=== an empty list assigned to [list-op]
sub f {}
() = f();
--- perl
2 stub
# -           <0> stub lPRM* ->-

=== print of a parenthesised list [absorbed]
print((1, 2));
--- perl

# 6     <@> print vKP ->7

# 6        <@> anonlist sKP*/1 ->7

my $r = {(a => 1)};

# 6        <@> anonhash sKP*/1 ->7

=== a reference to a parenthesised list [list-op]
my ($a, $b);
my $r = \($a, $b);
--- perl
1 list
2 ex-list
# -     <@> list vKP ->4
# -           <1> ex-list lKPRM ->6

=== a do block's parenthesised list [list-op]

--- perl
1 list
# 5              <@> list sKP ->6

=== a parenthesised lexical before an arrow subscript [scalar-op]
my $x;
my $r = ($x)->[0];
--- perl
2 ex-padsv
# -              <0> ex-padsv sPM/DREFAV ->5

=== a parenthesised arrow element [scalar-op]
my $x;
my $r = ($x->[0]);
--- perl
2 ex-aelem
# -        <1> ex-aelem sKP/2 ->6

=== a parenthesised keys [scalar-op]
my %h;
my $r = (keys %h);
--- perl

# -        <1> keys[t3] sKP/1 ->6

=== a doubly parenthesised sort [doubled]
my @a;
my @r = ((sort @a));
--- perl

# 8           <@> sort lKP ->9

=== a parenthesised scalar assignment [scalar-op]
my $x;
my $r = ($x = 1);
--- perl
2 sassign
# 7        <2> sassign sKPS/2 ->8
